correctness.rationale: For each q, Lucas gives a specific interior coefficient pair that is q-unit if neither n nor n−1 is a q-power. If n=q^a, the identity nu_q C(q^a,j)=a−nu_q(j) makes the minimum exactly 1. If n−1=q^b, Lucas isolates four q-unit binomial positions and forces a minimum min(2,b) except for (q,b)=(2,1),(2,2), with boundary or q^(b−1) witnesses. The proof covers n>=3 and all q; no infinite claim is inferred from tests. Actual packaged verify.py recomputes rows 3..600 and 5210 local minima through n=700 using a separate factorial-valuation algorithm; all passed.

value.rationale: A natural invariant in Dyck-path/Narayana peak enumeration is the exact common divisor of all nonendpoint peak counts. The result yields a complete uniform all-index classification and restricts all prime factors to prime powers among consecutive indices, with exact exponents, striking composite families G(q^b+1)=q^2 for most b>=2, and two sharp small binary exceptions. It strengthens a previously prime-index-only gcd theorem and is not a table recomputation or an arbitrary numerical slice; its exact sharp content can support divisibility and primitive-content questions for Narayana polynomials.
